mainTopic: Why not laundering is a bigger hardship than not bathing according to רבי יוסי, a warning about dirt, and why the sons of תלמידי חכמים often do not become תלמידי חכמים themselves.
overview: The גמרא finishes a challenge to רבי יוסי: if not laundering counts as suffering, shouldn't not bathing count even more? It answers that dirty clothes are worse, and proves this from שמואל's teaching about the dangers of grime. A message from ארץ ישראל follows: be careful about grime, learn Torah in a group, and value the sons of the poor, because Torah comes from them. The גמרא then asks why the sons of תלמידי חכמים often do not become תלמידי חכמים, and five אמוראים answer. רבינא's answer, that they do not first say a ברכה on the Torah, is proven from פסוקים in ירמיהו about why the land was destroyed. Next comes the story of איסי בר יהודה and ורדימוס, which finds the source for רבי יוסי's rule that a town's laundry comes before other people's lives in the word 'חייתם'. Finally, the גמרא asks whether, according to רבי יוסי, a husband can cancel bathing and grooming vows as matters between him and his wife. An attempted proof is rejected, and רב אדא בר אהבה and רב הונא disagree.

steps.title: Shouldn't the whole body count even more?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if not laundering clothes counts as suffering for רבי יוסי, then not bathing the whole body should certainly count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole body, all the more so?!
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a challenge that began just before this section. The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי could treat dirty clothes as real suffering without treating an unwashed body the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is a קל וחומר. Clothes are only on the outside, while bathing affects the whole body. So if a vow against laundering counts as עינוי נפש, a vow against bathing should count even more.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a reasoning from a smaller case to a bigger one)

phrases.english: The entire body — is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that refraining from laundering counts as suffering, while bathing apparently does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the body is more central than clothing, so the hardship of not bathing should be at least as great.

steps.title: Not laundering is the stronger hardship
steps.stepSummary: The answer is yes: for רבי יוסי, the suffering of not laundering is actually greater than the suffering of not bathing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Yes, laundering is stronger according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by flipping its starting assumption. Dirty clothes are really worse than a dirty body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that not bathing is the bigger hardship. The answer denies that assumption, so the 'all the more so' reasoning falls apart. The next step brings a source to back this up.

phrases.english: They say: Yes,
laundering is stronger according to Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: He means that going without laundering is the more serious suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִין, כְּבִיסָה אַלִּימָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise: the supposedly smaller case is actually the more severe one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not bathing the whole body is the greater suffering.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, dirty clothes are the greater suffering, so no קל וחומר follows.

steps.title: שמואל on the dangers of grime
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that grime on the head leads to blindness, grime on clothes leads to madness, and grime on the body leads to boils and sores.
steps.simpleTranslation: As שמואל said: Grime on the head leads to blindness. Grime on clothes leads to madness. Grime on the body leads to boils and sores.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's teaching to prove that dirty clothes are more harmful than a dirty body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Madness, which comes from dirty clothes, is far worse than skin sores, which come from a dirty body. This supports the answer that laundering is the stronger need.

phrases.english: As Shmuel said:
This grime of the head —
brings one to blindness;
grime of the clothes —
brings one to madness;
grime of the body —
brings one to boils and sores.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, a dirty-clothes vow is the more serious hardship, because dirty clothes lead to madness while a dirty body only leads to sores.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim that laundering is the stronger need.
steps.raayaObject: Not laundering is a worse hardship than not bathing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ranking of the harms caused by grime.

steps.title: A message from ארץ ישראל: three warnings
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of ארץ ישראל sent three warnings: be careful about grime, study Torah with a group, and care for the sons of the poor, because Torah will come from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: Be careful about grime. Be careful about studying in a group. Be careful with the sons of the poor, because Torah will come out from them. As it says, 'Water shall flow from his branches (מדליו)': from the poor ones, Torah will come out.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is grime, the גמרא quotes a message sent from ארץ ישראל that starts with grime. It then adds two more warnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first warning connects back to שמואל's teaching. The third warning reads מדליו ('his branches') as if it said מדלים ('from the poor'). Torah is compared to water, so the פסוק is read to mean Torah flows from the poor.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there (from ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: They sent from there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל, sending a message to בבל.

phrases.english: Be careful about grime.
Be careful about learning in a group.
Be careful with the sons of the poor,
for from them Torah will come forth,
as it is said: "Water shall flow from his branches,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:7. מדליו is read as if it said מדלים, 'from the poor.'

phrases.english: for from them Torah will come forth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the grime discussion to a related teaching that opens with grime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Be careful about grime, study in a group, and value the sons of the poor, because Torah comes from them.

steps.title: Why don't scholars' sons become scholars?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the sons of תלמידי חכמים usually do not become תלמידי חכמים themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason is it uncommon for תלמידי חכמים to have sons who become תלמידי חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: Following the idea that Torah comes from the poor, the גמרא asks the flip side. It is setting up a list of answers that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Torah comes from the sons of the poor, it seems Torah often does not pass down in scholars' families. The גמרא wants to know the reason for this.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין מְצוּיִין תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
phrases.english: And for what reason is it not common for Torah scholars
to have Torah scholars come out from their sons?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין מְצוּיִין תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the other side of 'Torah comes from the poor.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason scholars' sons often do not become scholars.

steps.title: רב יוסף: so Torah isn't seen as an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says this happens so people will not say that Torah is a family inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: So that they should not say Torah is their inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the first answer: it shows that Torah does not automatically pass from father to son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If scholars' sons always became scholars, Torah would look like a family possession. This way, everyone sees that Torah must be earned through effort.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ: תּוֹרָה יְרוּשָּׁה הִיא לָהֶם.
phrases.english: So that they should not say: Torah is an inheritance for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To prevent people from thinking Torah is a family inheritance.

steps.title: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי: so they won't act arrogantly
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says it is so the scholars' families will not act arrogantly toward the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת the son of רב אידי says: So that they will not be arrogant toward the community.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: it keeps scholars' families from feeling superior to everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If scholarship were guaranteed in a family, its members might look down on the public. Not passing it down protects against that pride.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, says:
So that they should not be arrogant toward the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To prevent them from being arrogant toward the community.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: because they lord over the community
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says it is because the sons lord over the community, so they are punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא says: Because they lord over the community.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: this is a result of how the sons actually behave, acting bossy toward the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת gave a reason to prevent arrogance before it happens. מר זוטרא says the arrogance already happens, and losing Torah is the consequence.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra says:
Because they lord over the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer, framed as a consequence rather than a prevention.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because they act domineering toward the community.

steps.title: רב אשי: because they call people donkeys
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says it is because they call ordinary people 'donkeys.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: Because they call people 'donkeys.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer: the problem is insulting ordinary people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a specific kind of disrespect: mocking those who are less learned. The punishment fits the behavior.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
Because they call people "donkeys."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because they insult ordinary people by calling them donkeys.

steps.title: רבינא: they don't make a ברכה on Torah first
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says it is because they do not first say a ברכה on the Torah before learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא says: Because they do not first bless over the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A fifth answer: they skip the ברכת התורה before studying. The גמרא will now bring a source for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers were about how they treat people. רבינא's answer is about how they treat the Torah itself: learning without first thanking הקב"ה for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Saying a ברכה over the Torah

phrases.english: Ravina says:
Because they do not bless over the Torah first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final answer in the list, which leads into a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because they do not say ברכת התורה before learning.

steps.title: The question no sage or prophet could answer
steps.stepSummary: To support רבינא, the גמרא quotes רב יהודה in the name of רב: the reason the land was destroyed was asked of the חכמים and the נביאים, and they could not explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What is meant by the פסוק 'Who is the wise man who will understand this'? This question was asked of the חכמים and the נביאים, and they did not explain it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof for רבינא's answer from a פסוק in ירמיהו. Steps 12 to 14 finish this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is why ארץ ישראל was destroyed. Not even the wise men or prophets could explain it. The answer, which comes next, will connect to not making a ברכה on the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written?

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Who is the wise man that may understand this" —
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 9:11. The פסוק continues by asking why the land was destroyed.

phrases.english: this matter was asked of the Sages and the prophets,
and they did not explain it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source for רבינא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: Not saying a ברכה on the Torah first is a serious failing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב, explaining ירמיהו 9:11–12 (completed in steps 12–14).

steps.title: ה׳ Himself explains why the land was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The prophets and sages could not explain why the land was destroyed, until ה׳ explained it in the next פסוק: 'Because they abandoned My Torah.'
steps.simpleTranslation: No one could explain it until the Holy One, Blessed be He, explained it Himself, as it is written: 'And ה׳ said: Because they have forsaken My Torah…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the proof it started in step 11. The answer to 'why was the land destroyed?' comes from ה׳ Himself in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the חכמים and the נביאים could not explain the destruction. Now the פסוק gives ה׳'s answer: they abandoned the Torah. The rest of the פסוק adds more phrases, and the next step notices that two of them seem to say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה׳)

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: until the Holy One, Blessed be He, explained it Himself,
as it is written: 'And ה׳ said:
Because they have forsaken My Torah, etc.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 9:12. The 'etc.' covers the rest of the פסוק, which the next step quotes.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof that step 11 started; it is completed in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that the problem was not saying a ברכה on the Torah first.

steps.title: The two phrases in the פסוק seem to say the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that 'they did not listen to My voice' and 'they did not walk in it' seem to be the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They did not listen to My voice' is the same as 'they did not walk in it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק seems to say the same thing twice. This sets up the next step, which explains what the extra phrase adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both phrases just mean 'they did not keep the Torah,' one of them is extra. The Torah does not waste words, so 'they did not walk in it' must mean something new.

keyTerms.meaning: they did not walk in it

phrases.english: That is the same as 'they did not listen to My voice,'
phrases.notes: Both of these phrases come from the end of the same פסוק, the part that was covered by 'etc.'

phrases.english: which is the same as 'they did not walk in it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ ״לֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּקוֹלִי״, הַיְינוּ ״לֹא הָלְכוּ בָּהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two phrases seem to say the same thing, so one of them looks extra.

steps.title: 'Not walking in it' means not saying a ברכה first
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב explains that the extra phrase means they did not say a ברכה on the Torah before learning. This supports רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It means that they did not first say a ברכה on the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the extra phrase in the פסוק: the people learned Torah, but they did not say a ברכה on it first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question of step 13 and also proves רבינא's answer from step 10. Scholars whose sons do not become scholars may have this same problem: they learn without first saying the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: the ברכה said before learning Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The land was destroyed because people learned Torah without first saying בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה. This proves רבינא's reason why scholars' sons are often not scholars.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for how important it is to say בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה before learning.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
that they do not first say a blessing over the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שֶׁאֵין מְבָרְכִין בַּתּוֹרָה תְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra phrase its own meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both phrases simply mean they did not keep the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not walking in it' means they learned without first saying a ברכה.

steps.title: איסי בר יהודה stays away from רבי יוסי's yeshiva
steps.stepSummary: איסי בר יהודה missed רבי יוסי's yeshiva for three days. When רבי יוסי's son ורדימוס asked why, he said he could not come because he did not understand רבי יוסי's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בר יהודה did not come to רבי יוסי's yeshiva for three days. ורדימוס, son of רבי יוסי, found him and asked: 'Why haven't you come to my father's study hall these three days?' He answered: 'Since I don't know your father's reasoning, how can I come?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that goes back to רבי יוסי's rule about laundry. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי was troubled by one of רבי יוסי's teachings and did not know where it came from. He felt he could not keep learning there without understanding it. His son ורדימוס now gets involved.

phrases.english: Isi bar Yehuda did not come
to the academy of Rabbi Yosei for three days.
Vardimus, son of Rabbi Yosei, found him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָתֵי מָר
phrases.english: and said to him: Why did the Master not come

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא דְּאַבָּא הָא תְּלָתָא יוֹמִין?
phrases.english: to Father's study hall these three days?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי טַעְמֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּךְ לָא יָדַעְנָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: When I do not know your father's reasoning,
how can I come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסִי בַּר יְהוּדָה לָא אֲתָא לִמְתִיבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that goes back to רבי יוסי's laundry rule from earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story that sets up a question about the source for one of רבי יוסי's rules.

steps.title: What is the source for 'laundry comes before other people's lives'?
steps.stepSummary: ורדימוס offers to help. איסי asks for the פסוק behind רבי יוסי's teaching that a town's own laundry comes before the lives of other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: ורדימוס said: 'Tell me what my father said that bothers you; maybe I know his reason.' איסי said: 'There is a ברייתא where רבי יוסי says their own laundry comes before other people's lives. Where do we learn this from a פסוק?'
steps.whatsHappening: איסי asks his real question: where in the Torah is רבי יוסי's surprising rule about laundry hinted?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule sounds very strange. How can washing clothes come before other people's lives? Because it is so surprising, איסי wants a פסוק to back it up.

keyTerms.meaning: that is taught in a ברייתא
from where do we know it in a פסוק?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֵימָא מָר מַאי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Let the Master say what he says,
phrases.notes: He means: tell me which of my father's teachings is bothering you.

phrases.english: perhaps I know his reasoning.
He said to him: That which is taught:
Rabbi Yosei says:
their own laundry takes precedence over the lives of others,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier ברייתא about a town's water: the town's own washing needs come before other people's needs.

phrases.english: from where do we have a verse for this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Says exactly what was bothering איסי in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in a פסוק for the rule that a town's laundry comes before other people's lives.

steps.title: ורדימוס quotes the פסוק about the land of the לוים
steps.stepSummary: ורדימוס answers with the פסוק about the open land around the cities of the לוים: it is for their animals, their belongings and 'all their חיה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it is written: 'And their open land shall be for their animals, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: ורדימוס starts his answer by quoting a פסוק. The next steps will explain which word in it teaches the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'חייתם' at the end of the פסוק. The גמרא will now try out different meanings for that word.

keyTerms.meaning: their open land around the city

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written:
'And their open land shall be for their animals, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:3. The 'etc.' covers 'and for their belongings and for all their חיה,' and that last word is the one that matters here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering איסי's question from step 16.

steps.title: 'חייתם' cannot mean wild animals
steps.stepSummary: If 'חייתם' meant wild animals, it would be extra, because wild animals are already included in 'animals.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'their חיה' mean? If you say it means wild animals, aren't wild animals already included in 'animals'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple meaning of 'חייתם', wild animals, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said 'their animals,' which covers wild animals too. So 'חייתם' must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: their חיה, a word that can mean wild animals or life

phrases.english: What is 'their beasts'?
If we say an actual wild animal —
isn't a wild animal included in the category of animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the key word in the פסוק of step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'חייתם' as wild animals
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would make the word extra, since animals were already mentioned.

steps.title: 'Their actual lives' is too obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'חייתם' means their actual lives, then rejects it because that is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'חייתם' mean? Their actual lives. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second meaning, 'their life,' and rejects that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of course the לוים were given cities so they could live in them, so the Torah would not need to say so. The word must mean something besides plain living.

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'their beasts'?
Their actual lives.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a second meaning after step 18 rejected the first.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'חייתם' as basic living
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah would not need to say something so obvious.

steps.title: 'חייתם' means laundry, which is needed to live comfortably
steps.stepSummary: The word must mean laundry, because dirty clothes cause real pain. That is why a town's laundry counts as part of its 'life' and comes before other people's needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean laundry, since there is real suffering from grime?
steps.whatsHappening: ורדימוס gives the final meaning: 'חייתם' refers to washing clothes. This is the source איסי was looking for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing dirty clothes causes real suffering, so clean clothes are part of a livable life. Since the Torah calls laundry part of the לוים's 'life,' a town's own laundry comes before the needs of others.

keyTerms.meaning: grime, the dirt of unwashed clothes

steps.whatToRemember: The source for רבי יוסי's rule is 'וּלְכֹל חַיָּתָם'. Wild animals and plain living do not fit the word, so it means laundry, because dirty clothes cause real suffering.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not laundering,
since there is the pain caused by grime?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 18 and 19 rule out two meanings, this gives the meaning that works.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'חייתם' means laundry. This is the source for רבי יוסי's rule that a town's own laundry comes before other people's lives.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יוסי says these are not vows of affliction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the משנה: vows about bathing or grooming are not נדרי עינוי נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: These are not vows of affliction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי יוסי's words. This sets up a question about them in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי holds that vows about bathing or grooming do not cause real suffering. So a husband cannot cancel them for the reason of עינוי נפש.

keyTerms.meaning: vows that cause personal suffering, which a husband may cancel

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
These are not vows of affliction.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the vows in the משנה about bathing and grooming.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵין אֵלּוּ נִדְרֵי עִינּוּי נֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the story to the words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, bathing and grooming vows are not נדרי עינוי נפש.

steps.title: Can the husband cancel them for a different reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי יוסי, can a husband still cancel these vows because they affect the relationship between him and his wife?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: According to רבי יוסי, can the husband cancel these vows because they are matters between him and her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether there is a second reason that would still let the husband cancel these vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can cancel two kinds of vows: vows of suffering, and vows that affect the two of them, דברים שבינו לבינה. רבי יוסי ruled out the first kind for these vows. The question is whether they still fit the second kind.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked to them, the חכמים
matters between him and her, things affecting the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'it is not a vow of affliction' does not mean 'the husband cannot cancel it.' There is a second, separate reason a husband may cancel a vow.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them: According to Rabbi Yosei,
what is the law as to whether he can nullify
because of matters between him and her?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, מַהוּ שֶׁיָּפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the limits of רבי יוסי's ruling quoted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי lets the husband cancel these vows as דברים שבינו לבינה.

steps.title: An attempted proof from רבי יוסי's wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from רבי יוסי's own words. He only said these are not vows of affliction, which suggests they do count as matters between husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי said, 'These are not vows of affliction.' This means that they are matters between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question by reading רבי יוסי's words carefully: he only took away one reason for cancelling. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said these are 'not vows of affliction,' not 'they cannot be cancelled at all.' That suggests the other reason still applies, so the husband can cancel them as דברים שבינו לבינה.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yosei said:
These are not vows of affliction.
But they are matters between him and her.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי did not say this out loud. The גמרא is drawing it from the fact that he only ruled out vows of affliction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggested (and rejected in step 24): since רבי יוסי only ruled out vows of affliction, these vows would count as דברים שבינו לבינה.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי יוסי the husband can cancel these vows as דברים שבינו לבינה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רבי יוסי in the משנה: 'אין אלו נדרי עינוי נפש'.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי was only arguing on the חכמים' terms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 23. רבי יוסי may hold these vows are not even matters between husband and wife. He was only telling the חכמים that, even by their own approach, these are not vows of affliction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps רבי יוסי was speaking to the חכמים according to their view: 'In my view, these are not even matters between him and her. But you say they are vows of affliction, so at least agree with me that they are not vows of affliction.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof it just brought. רבי יוסי's wording does not prove he thinks these vows count as matters between husband and wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the גמרא reasoned that since רבי יוסי only denied 'affliction', he must agree to 'between him and her'. Now it explains that he only argued against the חכמים' claim, one step at a time. His silence about 'between him and her' does not mean he agrees to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe (opens a possible other reading)
He was speaking to them according to their own view
According to me, in my view
Agree with me (at least on this point)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as רבי יוסי saying the vows ARE matters between husband and wife. He is only meeting the חכמים halfway in an argument, so these words don't show his own view. Step 26 brings the אמוראים' dispute about it.

phrases.english: Perhaps he was speaking to them according to their view.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוסי, and 'them' are the חכמים he was arguing with in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי אֲפִילּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ לָא הָוַיִין.
phrases.english: According to me, they are not even matters between him and her.
But according to you, who say
that they are vows of affliction,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹדוֹ לִי דְּאֵין אֵלּוּ נִדְרֵי עִינּוּי נֶפֶשׁ.
phrases.english: agree with me that these are not vows of affliction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference from רבי יוסי's wording made in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from step 23 that רבי יוסי holds these are matters between husband and wife.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's answer may only be an argument on the חכמים' terms ('even by your view'), so it tells us nothing about his own view.

steps.title: So what does רבי יוסי hold?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the proof has been rejected, the גמרא asks its question again: what is the law according to רבי יוסי?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: This one word sets up the next move. The question from step 22 is open again, and the גמרא is about to bring a dispute about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 23 and 24 cancel each other out, so we are back where we started. The גמרא now turns to what later אמוראים said about it.

phrases.english: What [is the law]?
phrases.notes: This brings back the question from step 22: can the husband cancel these vows according to רבי יוסי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected in step 24, the original question is asked again.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to רבי יוסי, a husband can cancel bathing and grooming vows as matters between him and his wife.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה says he can cancel, רב הונא says he cannot
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree about רבי יוסי's view. רב אדא בר אהבה says the husband can cancel these vows, and רב הונא says he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה says: he can cancel. רב הונא says: he cannot cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a dispute between two אמוראים about the open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה holds that, for רבי יוסי, these vows are matters between husband and wife, so the husband can cancel them. רב הונא holds they are not, so the husband has no power to cancel them. This lines up with the two readings of רבי יוסי from steps 23 and 24.

keyTerms.meaning: He cancels (the husband can cancel the vow)
An אמורא who says the husband can cancel
An אמורא who says the husband cannot cancel

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's view on bathing and grooming vows is disputed. רב אדא בר אהבה says the husband can cancel them, and רב הונא says he cannot.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אוֹמֵר: מֵפֵר,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava says: He can cancel [these vows],
Rav Huna says: He cannot cancel [them].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אוֹמֵר: מֵפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reopened question from step 25 by bringing a dispute between אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי: רב אדא בר אהבה says the husband can cancel bathing and grooming vows, and רב הונא says he cannot.
